Company: SkyHop Airlines

US regional airline (~3,500 employees) flying short domestic routes from hubs in Denver and Salt Lake City. Fleet is 60 Embraer E175 jets and 25 Airbus A320-family jets (A319 and A320). Sells tickets online and at airports, charges bag fees, and runs its own maintenance hangar. Does not fly Boeing aircraft, Airbus A220/A350, or helicopters; no cargo-only flights, no international routes.

Rules that APPLY:
- FAA airworthiness directives for Embraer E175 (ERJ 170 family) or Airbus A319/A320, and their engines
- FAA rules for airline operations, pilots, crew rest and drug/alcohol testing
- DOT consumer rules for airline passengers (refunds, fees, accessibility)
- Airspace or airport rules at Denver or Salt Lake City, and airport fees charged to passengers
- TSA security rules for airlines

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Airworthiness directives for aircraft models we do not fly (Boeing, A220, A350, business jets, small planes, helicopters)
- Airspace changes at airports we do not serve
- Commercial space launches, drones, air-traffic-control equipment
- Banking, food, pharmacy, energy

Affected areas and owners:
- maintenance: Airworthiness directives, inspections, parts for our fleet → Carlos Mendez (Director of Maintenance)
- flight-ops: Flight operations, pilots and crew rules, airspace at our hubs → Jenna Holt (Flight Operations)
- customers: Passenger rights, refunds, fees, accessibility (DOT) → Omar Haddad (Customer Policy)
- safety-security: Drug/alcohol testing, TSA security, safety programs → Grace Liu (Safety & Security)

- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/22/2026-21590/airworthiness-directives-general-electric-company-engines
- **Published:** 2026-10-22, as a final rule (AD 2026-21-11).
- **Key deadline:** The AD is effective November 27, 2026.
- **Tier:** Critical. It is a final rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-10-23.

- **Action:** Check the 60 E175 engine fleet against the AD's EEC FADEC part-number applicability. Schedule the software replacement. Check for the memory upgrade that some engines need. The FAA says this work can be done during regularly scheduled maintenance.

- **Airbus SAS AD 2026-21331 (published 10/19, final rule, effective Nov 23, 2026):** The snippets I retrieved did not show which Airbus models it covers. If it does apply, it would be Critical (maintenance).

markdown:
# Regulatory triage — SkyHop Airlines
Window 2026-10-19 → 2026-10-23 · as of 2026-10-23 · 1 items

## Critical (1)

- **Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines** [web search — verify]
  - Check the 60 E175 engine fleet against the AD's EEC FADEC part-number applicability, schedule the software replacement, and check for the memory upgrade some engines need; the FAA says this can be done during regularly scheduled maintenance. Owner: Carlos Mendez.
  - Dates: effective 2026-11-27 ✓ · Owner: Carlos Mendez (Director of Maintenance) · Areas: maintenance
  - 91 FR 66631 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/22/2026-21590/airworthiness-directives-general-electric-company-engines

votes.why: Gives the maintenance director a concrete next step: check the fleet against the AD's applicability and schedule the software replacement.
Adds details the title, reason and rubric don't support: a '60' engine fleet count, a memory upgrade some engines need, and an FAA statement that the work fits regularly scheduled maintenance.
Conveys that the E175 fleet's engines need the FADEC engine-control software replaced, covering both mustMention points.
It gives Carlos several tasks rather than one concrete next step and uses unexplained jargon such as “EEC FADEC part-number applicability.”
The provided material does not support the 60-engine count, the memory-upgrade claim, or the statement that the FAA says the work can be done during scheduled maintenance.
It identifies the E175 fleet and calls for replacing the FADEC engine-control software on affected engines.
The action uses plain operational language and gives Carlos Mendez a clear next step to check fleet applicability and schedule the software update.

The action introduces several claims unsupported by the title, reason, or rubric, including a 60-engine fleet count, a memory upgrade requirement, and FAA permission to use regularly scheduled maintenance.
The action conveys both key points by stating that the E175 engine fleet is affected and requires EEC FADEC software replacement.
